findings.title: Public file-request upload is permission-gated and unreachable for anonymous uploaders
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/file-requests.ts:109-118 — POST /public/:token/upload is registered without requirePermission; authorization is the token row itself

supabase/migrations/5302430_file_request_uploads.sql:15-60 — table with org-member SELECT RLS, FK cascade

findings.title: `avatars` bucket is used by code but declared nowhere with no storage RLS policy
evidence: supabase/migrations/5302433_avatars_bucket_policies.sql:30-31 — `insert into storage.buckets ('avatars', public=true)`

apps/api/src/routes/profiles.ts:216-229 — uploads to `<userId>/avatar.<ext>` and returns getPublicUrl

findings.title: Free-form `storageBucket`/`storagePath` on create/update allows signing arbitrary in-bucket objects
evidence: apps/api/src/validators/document.ts:24-31 — storageBucket is z.literal("documents"); storagePath must match `^[0-9a-fA-F-]{36}/[^/]+$`
apps/api/src/routes/documents.ts:267-272,516-521 — the path's first segment must equal the document's/caller's organization id
apps/api/src/routes/documents.ts:346-352 — upload bucket pinned server-side; path server-derived
apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/documents/page.tsx:208-217,273-280 — admin path flow validates the org prefix client-side
apps/api/src/__tests__/documents.test.ts:189-252,283-304 — tests reject foreign buckets and foreign-org prefixes

findings.title: No content/AV scanning and no bucket-level MIME/size limits on the documents bucket
evidence: grep -rni "clamav|virus|malware|antivirus|quarantine" apps/ — no upload-scanning code (matches are DMARC/blog copy)
supabase/migrations/5302026_...corrected.v3.sql:2297-2299 — documents bucket inserted with (id,name,public) only; no allowed_mime_types/file_size_limit
supabase/config.toml.production.example:66 — only a global file_size_limit="25MiB"
apps/api/src/routes/documents.ts:118-133,324-333 — all MIME/size/content enforcement lives in the Express process
findings.impact: Nothing inspects file contents for malware and the bucket itself accepts any object type/size through any storage path; an infected upload can propagate to other users on download.
findings.recommendation: Add bucket-level allowed_mime_types/file_size_limit in a migration and an asynchronous scan-on-upload hook (e.g. ClamAV sidecar) with quarantine; record scan status on the document row.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: no scan code and no bucket-level limits found; see also the new direct-write bypass finding.

findings.title: No backup or restore path for uploaded objects (durability for files)
evidence: scripts/backup-storage.sh:31,86-105 — mirrors documents/avatars/logos to S3/Spaces with a manifest and optional AES-256-CBC encryption
scripts/restore-storage.sh:43-121 — restore with --dry-run, .enc decryption, and upsert control
.github/workflows/storage-backup.yml:18-56 — daily 05:00 UTC schedule + manual dispatch + failure notification
docs/RTO_RPO.md:11,19,25 — storage RPO ≤24h / RTO 1h and the paired DB+storage restore procedure
findings.impact: Uploaded documents/avatars/logos now have a scheduled offsite mirror and a documented restore path; a DB-only restore no longer implies permanent object loss.
findings.recommendation: No action on the code; exercise the restore path (see the new storage-restore-drill finding).
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: backup script + workflow + restore script + RTO/RPO docs present. Residual: no storage restore has been exercised (no CI storage restore test; db-restore-test.yml covers Postgres only) — tracked as a new P3.

findings.title: Content sniffing does not cover Office, archive, text/JSON, or polyglot payloads
evidence: apps/api/src/lib/upload-validation.ts:8-18 — looksLikeMarkup inspects only the first 512 bytes
apps/api/src/lib/upload-validation.ts:40-81 — validateUploadContent only byte-sniffs image/* and application/pdf
apps/api/src/routes/documents.ts:97-116 — ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES includes Office, zip/gzip, JSON, plain, CSV, RTF
apps/api/src/routes/file-requests.ts:17-34 — same families allowed on the public intake
findings.impact: Files declared as Office/zip/JSON/text are stored without content verification, and a leading-padding polyglot can evade the 512-byte head check; stored markup remains a latent XSS/malware enabler.
findings.recommendation: Sniff zip/OOXML (PK\x03\x04) and gzip (\x1f\x8b) magic, enforce declared-vs-detected agreement for all families, and scan the full buffer (not just 512 bytes) for markup.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: upload-validation.ts still covers only image/PDF plus a 512-byte markup head; no unit tests exist for it (see test-gap finding).

findings.title: CSV exports do not neutralize formula injection and default to all rows when `organization_id` is omitted
evidence: apps/api/src/lib/csv.ts:16-30 — escapeCsvValue prefixes ' for values starting with = + - @ tab/CR (numeric values untouched)
apps/api/src/routes/tickets.ts:60-71, projects.ts:62-69, audit.ts:72-78 — resolveAdminTenantScope + applyRequestedOrg + applyOrgScope
apps/api/src/routes/{proposals,findings,domain-monitors,assets,approvals}.ts — same scoped export pattern
apps/api/src/routes/satisfaction-pulse-widget.ts:93-100, client-onboarding-command-center.ts:86-96 — use escapeCsvValue with org-scoped services
apps/api/src/__tests__/csv.test.ts:4-35 — formula-guard tests
findings.impact: Exported CSVs can no longer execute injected formulas, and exports cannot default to all tenants.
findings.recommendation: No action; optionally add Cache-Control: private, no-store to export responses.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: guard present in csv.ts and applied by all 10 export surfaces; tenant scoping via admin-scope helpers; fix commit 0dd81973 is an ancestor.

findings.title: Share endpoint has no per-token rate limit
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/documents.ts:146-204 — GET /shares/:token has no route-level limiter
apps/api/src/app.ts:125-146 — only the global IP limiter (300/15m) applies to the path
apps/api/src/middleware/rate-limit.ts — no token-keyed limiter exists
findings.impact: A leaked share token can be fetched at the global rate and consume the access_count quickly; tokens are 32 random bytes so enumeration is infeasible.
findings.recommendation: Add a limiter keyed by sha256(token) with a short window on the share route.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: unchanged; global IP limiter remains the only throttle.

findings.title: Client logo accept list still advertises SVG that the server rejects
evidence: apps/web/components/admin/OrgBrandingForm.tsx:102 — accept="image/png,image/jpeg,image/svg+xml"
apps/web/components/admin/OrgBrandingForm.tsx:113 — helper text "PNG, JPG, or SVG. 5MB max."
apps/api/src/routes/organizations.ts:43-51 — resolveImageUpload rejects image/svg+xml (jpeg/png/webp/gif only)

findings.recommendation: Update accept to image/png,image/jpeg,image/webp,image/gif and correct the helper text.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: mismatch unchanged at OrgBrandingForm.tsx:102,113 vs organizations.ts:43-51.

findings.title: Documentation drift on file types and size limits; no documents/upload runbook
evidence: docs/modules/documents.md, docs/modules/file-requests.md, docs/runbooks/secure-file-request.md, docs/features/secure-file-request.md — module docs and a runbook now exist
docs/ARCHITECTURAL_ANALYSIS.md:274 — still says "documents (private, 50MB)" while documents.ts:120 enforces 2MB
docs/modules/documents.md endpoint table lists routes that do not exist (POST /:id/upload, GET /:id/download, POST /:id/share, POST /bulk)
apps/api/src/validators/file-requests.ts:7 — default maxFileSizeMb=50 exceeds the 25MB multer cap at file-requests.ts:60
findings.impact: Operators and future agents will mis-state capacity and endpoint behaviour; per-request size settings above 25MB are silently unreachable.
findings.recommendation: Reconcile documented limits with the constants, fix the documents endpoint table, document the upload/download routes, and publish a bucket matrix with signed-URL/share semantics.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: docs/runbook now exist (previous gap closed) but size claims and endpoint tables still drift.

findings.title: Document download authorization bypasses the `can_read_document` visibility model
evidence: supabase/migrations/5302026_...corrected.v3.sql:2181-2187 — documents SELECT policy is `can_read_document(id)`
supabase/migrations/5302026_...corrected.v3.sql:740-790 — can_read_document restricts private (uploader/document_permissions) and internal (uploader/manage/roles) documents
apps/api/src/routes/documents.ts:209-258 — list/get apply no visibility filter and run on the scoped client
apps/api/src/routes/documents.ts:603-629 — POST /:id/signed-url requires documents:create and an org predicate only; no visibility/ACL check

apps/api/src/services/supabase.ts:203-226 — getScopedClient falls back to the service-role client unless RLS_*_ENABLED lists the module; infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:108-109 defaults both to empty
supabase/migrations/5302128_role_catalog_expansion.sql:76 — the engineer role is granted documents create/edit
findings.impact: Any approved org member (and any role with documents:create such as engineer) can list metadata for and mint download URLs for private/internal documents they are not entitled to view; document_permissions is unenforced through the primary client path.
findings.recommendation: Apply the can_read_document predicate to list/get/signed-url/version endpoints (SQL filter or RPC), authorize downloads with documents:view instead of documents:create, and add documents to the RLS allow-lists where the user-scoped client is used; add private/internal cross-role tests.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d. Code paths captured statically; runtime RLS_READS_ENABLED/RLS_WRITES_ENABLED values are Unknown (not in repo), so live impact depends on deployment config. Overlaps SEC/ACM/RLS ownership — referenced, not duplicated.

findings.title: Members with `documents:create` can write objects straight to the documents bucket, bypassing upload validation
evidence: supabase/migrations/5302129_supabase_rls_audit_fixes.sql:718-733 — insert policy allows any approved member with documents:create to insert objects whose path starts with their org UUID
supabase/migrations/5302026_...corrected.v3.sql:2297-2299 — bucket declared without allowed_mime_types/file_size_limit
apps/api/src/routes/documents.ts:118-133,324-333 — MIME allowlist, 2MB cap and byte sniffing exist only in the Express handler
apps/api/src/routes/profiles.ts:34-44 — the avatar path shows the intended MIME→extension hardening that direct writes skip
findings.impact: A member with a Supabase access token (and the project URL/anon key, which are not published by this repo) can store markup or oversized files directly in the private bucket; API-side validation never runs, undercutting the FILE-P2-003/005 controls.
findings.recommendation: Set bucket-level allowed_mime_types/file_size_limit and/or remove the authenticated insert policy so all writes flow through the API (service role); keep the org-prefix check as defense in depth.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d; enforcement half of FILE-P2-003. Precondition: caller must know the Supabase project URL/anon key (Unknown whether reachable from the client bundle).

findings.title: Storage restore path exists but has never been exercised
evidence: .github/workflows/db-restore-test.yml:1-30 — the weekly restore test covers the database only; no storage equivalent exists
.github/workflows/storage-backup.yml:18-56 — backup is scheduled (05:00 UTC) but performs no restore verification
docs/RTO_RPO.md:11 — claims a storage RTO of 1 hour; docs/RTO_RPO.md:44-47 — states targets are meaningful only when exercised
findings.impact: The storage recovery path is configured but not proven; an actual bucket-loss event could reveal archive/decrypt/upload defects with no prior drill evidence.
findings.recommendation: Add a weekly or quarterly storage restore test (restore into a scratch bucket, or validate the manifest object count and a sample checksum), or record a dated manual drill artifact.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d; cross-ref DR-P1-001 (prompt 32). Delivery vs configuration: recorded as not exercised.

findings.title: Share revocation does not invalidate already-issued signed URLs
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/documents.ts:159-165 — revocation/expiry/max-access are evaluated only when GET /shares/:token is called
apps/api/src/routes/documents.ts:171-173 — a 3600s signed URL is minted at that moment; the storage layer has no revocation handle
apps/api/src/routes/documents.ts:620,851 — the authenticated signed-url endpoints likewise mint 3600s URLs with no disposition option
findings.impact: A signed URL already handed to a recipient keeps working for up to one hour after the share link is revoked or expires.
findings.recommendation: Shorten share-URL lifetime (e.g. 5-15 minutes), serve shares via an API download endpoint that re-checks revocation, or document the residual window in the share threat model.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d. Inherent to signed URLs; max_access accounting still applies.

findings.title: Oversized uploads return 500 instead of a validation error
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/documents.ts:118-121 — multer fileSize 2MB; apps/api/src/routes/file-requests.ts:58-60 25MB; profiles.ts:14-16 2MB; organizations.ts:23-25 5MB
apps/api/src/middleware/error.ts:46-50 — MulterError is not mapped, so it falls through to the generic 500 handler
findings.impact: Exceeding any upload cap yields 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of a 400/413 validation message, breaking the documented error contract and creating Sentry noise.
findings.recommendation: Map MulterError (LIMIT_FILE_SIZE, LIMIT_UNEXPECTED_FILE) to a 400/413 VALIDATION response in middleware/error.ts.

findings.title: File-domain test gaps: no upload-validation unit tests and no file-request download coverage
evidence: apps/api/src/__tests__/ — csv.test.ts and validators.test.ts exist; no upload-validation.test.ts (grep validateUploadContent in tests returns nothing)
apps/api/src/__tests__/file-requests.test.ts:352-361 — the only markup-rejection test (route level); no image/PDF magic-byte cases
apps/api/src/routes/file-requests.ts:338-397 — the uploads list/signed-URL endpoints have no tests, including cross-org denial
apps/web/e2e/portal/document-preview.spec.ts:1-8 — a render smoke test only, no preview/download assertions
findings.impact: The load-bearing byte-sniffing control and the newly added intake download endpoints have no regression protection; a future refactor could silently weaken them.
findings.recommendation: Unit-test looksLikeMarkup/sniffImageType/validateUploadContent (including padded payloads), integration-test intake list/signed-URL with a foreign org (404), and extend the preview e2e.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d; documents/versions/bulk cross-tenant tests already exist and should be kept.

findings.title: Previews render untrusted files inline without sandbox or disposition controls
evidence: apps/web/components/DocumentPreview.tsx:27-33 — PDF rendered in an iframe with no sandbox attribute
apps/web/components/DocumentPreview.tsx:53-62 — text/CSV/JSON rendered in an iframe with no sandbox attribute
apps/web/components/DocumentPreview.tsx:14 — the extension list still treats svg as an image type

apps/api/src/routes/documents.ts:618-620 and file-requests.ts:387-389 — createSignedUrl(path, 3600) without a download option, so objects are served inline (Supabase default; not reproduced at runtime)
findings.impact: If content validation is bypassed (direct-write finding) or evaded (polyglot finding), markup could render from the storage origin inside an unsandboxed frame; no disposition control exists for non-previewable types.
findings.recommendation: Add sandbox to the preview iframes, drop svg from the image branch, and pass download/Content-Disposition for types that should never render inline.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d; extends the previous FILE-011 preview concern with current evidence.

report:
# File Upload and Download Security Audit

## Audit Metadata

- Audit name: repo-deep-dive
- Run: `mainecybertech-20261011-0426-full-main-8d299b8`
- Repository: `MaineCyberTech/mainecybertech` (read-only worktree `/tmp/opencode/mct-audit-target`)
- Branch: `main`
- Commit SHA: `8d299b8d`
- Generated at: 2026-10-11
- Auditor: OpenCode audit subagent (prompt 28, area code FILE)
- Area code: FILE
- Output path (pack): `docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/{run}/28_file_upload_download_security_audit.md`
- Scope limitations:
  - Static, repository-only review. No API was started, no bucket was contacted, no object was uploaded/downloaded. RLS behaviour, bucket `public` flags, and storage enforcement are read from committed SQL/config.
  - Live Supabase settings (`RLS_READS_ENABLED`/`RLS_WRITES_ENABLED`, bucket `file_size_limit`/`allowed_mime_types`, plan tier) are not in the repository → `Unknown`.
  - IDs are assigned later by the aggregator; verification rows keep the exact titles of the previous run's register rows.
  - Cross-referenced, not duplicated: SEC/ACM/RLS (prompt 06/24/37), DR (prompt 32), CHAIN (prompt 45).

## Scope

Reviewed: document upload/create/update/delete routes, version history and version signed URLs, share links (create/list/update/delete/public access), public file-request intake and its download endpoints, avatar/logo uploads, storage bucket declarations and `storage.objects` RLS policies, upload content validation, CSV/JSON exports, orphan cleanup, storage backup/restore, previews, rate limiting, and the corresponding tests/docs.

Not reviewed: live bucket state/CDN behaviour, Supabase dashboard settings, non-file exports beyond the shared CSV helper (owned by other domains), and billing/retention product modules (owned by prompts 07/29).

## Executive Summary

The file subsystem at `8d299b8d` is materially hardened. All three previous P1s and four of the previous P2s are fixed and re-verified with current-commit evidence: anonymous file-request uploads are token-authorized with org-prefixed paths and a persisted `file_request_uploads` row plus org-authorized list/signed-URL endpoints; document version objects are retained and reconciled by orphan cleanup; the `avatars` bucket is declared with owner-scoped policies; document `storageBucket`/`storagePath` are constrained and org-checked; and every CSV export now applies a formula-injection guard with a mandatory tenant scope.

Remaining risks concentrate in enforcement depth rather than feature gaps:

1. **Download authorization does not implement the document visibility model.** The DB defines `can_read_document` (private/internal/public + `document_permissions`) and the `documents` table/storage SELECT policies use it, but the API routes run on the service-role client by default and only check `documents:create` + org. Any org member with upload rights can list and sign `private`/`internal` documents. (New, P2.)
2. **No AV/content scanning and no bucket-level MIME/size limits** (still open FILE-P2-003); the documents-bucket RLS *allows* approved members to insert objects directly, so API validation is bypassable and oversized/markup content can be stored without ever touching `validateUploadContent`. (New, P2, plus still-open FILE-P2-005.)
3. **Durability is configured but unproven:** storage backup/restore scripts and a daily workflow exist (FILE-P2-004 fixed), yet no storage restore has ever been exercised and `db-restore-test` covers only Postgres. (New, P3.)

Strengths to preserve: shared byte-sniffing validator, pinned bucket, unique non-upsert paths, atomic file-request slot claim/release with slot tokens, retained version history with version signed URLs, avatars bucket policies, CSV guard + tenant scoping, fail-closed orphan cleanup with folder/recursion guards, OpenAPI coverage of the new endpoints, and real cross-tenant API tests for documents.

- Status: `open` (new; cross-ref DR-P1-001).

### Finding: Share revocation does not invalidate already-issued signed URLs

- Severity: P3
- Confidence: Medium
- Area: FILE
- Evidence:
  - `apps/api/src/routes/documents.ts:159-165` — revocation/expiry/max-access are checked only when the share endpoint is called.
  - `apps/api/src/routes/documents.ts:171-173` — a 3600s signed URL is minted at that moment; no revocation handle exists at the storage layer.
- What is happening: after revocation, a URL already handed out keeps working for up to one hour.
- Recommended fix: shorten share-URL lifetime (e.g. 5–15 minutes), serve shares through an API download endpoint that re-checks revocation, or document the residual window.
- Status: `open` (new).

### Finding: Oversized uploads return 500 instead of a validation error

- Severity: P3
- Confidence: High
- Area: FILE
- Evidence:
  - `apps/api/src/routes/documents.ts:118-121` — multer `fileSize: 2MB`.
  - `apps/api/src/routes/file-requests.ts:58-60` (25MB), `profiles.ts:14-16` (2MB), `organizations.ts:23-25` (5MB).
  - `apps/api/src/middleware/error.ts:46-50` — `MulterError` is not mapped, so it falls through to the generic 500 handler.
- What is happening: exceeding a size cap yields `500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` instead of 400/413.
- Recommended fix: map `MulterError` (`LIMIT_FILE_SIZE`, `LIMIT_UNEXPECTED_FILE`) to a 400/413 `VALIDATION` response.
- Status: `open` (new).

### Finding: File-domain test gaps: no upload-validation unit tests and no file-request download coverage

- Severity: P3
- Confidence: High
- Area: FILE
- Evidence:
  - `apps/api/src/__tests__/` — `csv.test.ts` and `validators.test.ts` exist; no `upload-validation.test.ts`; `grep validateUploadContent apps/api/src/__tests__` returns nothing.
  - `apps/api/src/__tests__/file-requests.test.ts:352-361` — the only markup-rejection test (route level); no image/PDF magic-byte cases.
  - `apps/api/src/routes/file-requests.ts:338-397` — download endpoints have no tests (including cross-org denial).
  - `apps/web/e2e/portal/document-preview.spec.ts:1-8` — render smoke test only.
- Recommended fix: unit-test `looksLikeMarkup`/`sniffImageType`/`validateUploadContent` (including padded payloads), integration-test the intake list/signed-URL endpoints with a foreign org (404), and extend the e2e preview test.
- Status: `open` (new).

### Finding: Previews render untrusted files inline without sandbox or disposition controls

- Severity: P3
- Confidence: Medium
- Area: FILE
- Evidence:
  - `apps/web/components/DocumentPreview.tsx:27-33` — PDF rendered in an `<iframe>` with no `sandbox`.
  - `apps/web/components/DocumentPreview.tsx:53-62` — text/CSV/JSON rendered in an `<iframe>` with no `sandbox`.
  - `apps/web/components/DocumentPreview.tsx:14` — extension list still treats `svg` as an image.
  - `apps/api/src/routes/documents.ts:618-620`, `file-requests.ts:387-389` — `createSignedUrl(path, 3600)` without a `download` option, so objects are served inline (Supabase default; not reproduced at runtime).
- What is happening: if content validation is bypassed (previous finding) or evaded (FILE-P2-005), markup can be rendered from the storage origin inside an unsandboxed frame.
- Recommended fix: add `sandbox` to the iframes, drop `svg` from the image branch, and pass `download`/`Content-Disposition` for non-previewable types.
- Status: `open` (new).
